fixes.explanation: Herod is a name that shows up other places in the Gospels (Mark 8:15), but not here. In this verse Jesus says, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees…” (Luke 12:1). I think that one is easy to mix up when a warning about leaven is already rolling around in your head. Same dough, different name on the bag.

Jesus doesn't name the Sadducees in this warning. He says, “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees…” (Luke 12:1). He even says what that leaven is: “…which is hypocrisy.” Pick the group He actually names, friend.

Right, baker. Jesus says, “There is nothing concealed that will not be disclosed, and nothing hidden that will not be made known.” (Luke 12:2). No exceptions on that list. I once tried hiding a burnt batch under a dish towel, and the smell told on me before the timer even stopped.

Jesus doesn't say that here. After those who kill the body, He says they “…can do no more.” (Luke 12:4). He gives no timing and no verdict on them in this verse. Judged at once is a big claim for a sentence that stops right there.
That sounds like a neat ending, friend, but Jesus doesn't say it. He says those who kill the body “…can do no more.” (Luke 12:4). Nothing about regret is in the verse.

Jesus mentions the Pharisees back in verse 1, but He doesn't point to them here. He says, “Fear the One who, after you have been killed, has authority to throw you into hell.” (Luke 12:5). The one to fear has authority beyond the killing of the body. That's a different level than any person.

I get why that pick looks good, friend. But Jesus says the Son of Man “…will also confess him before the angels of God.” (Luke 12:8). Confessing Him happens before men, and His confessing them happens before the angels of God. Different rooms, baker.

That's it, baker. Jesus says, “…whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.” (Luke 12:10). Just before that, He says everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven. That's a serious line, friend.

Moses is a big name, baker, but Jesus doesn't name him here. He says, “…whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.” (Luke 12:10). Even a famous name can't take the Holy Spirit's spot in that sentence.

The prophets aren't named in this verse, friend. Jesus says everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, “…but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.” (Luke 12:10). The Holy Spirit is the one He points to.

Free sounds like the happy ending, baker, and I'd pick it too. But Jesus says, “…do not worry about how to defend yourselves or what to say.” (Luke 12:11). Defending is the worry He lifts off them, and I'd gladly hand that one over.
